{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABa9I_oA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhEihtc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 85, "title": "Implement firmware-driven ISO9660 boot-file discovery and loading through Saturn CD hardware", "body": "## Problem

[Issue #83 / PR #84](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/84) established a real, reproducible **ExternalBios → SMPC/SCU/CD → disc executable handoff**, with an original 512 KiB synthetic ROM and an original Saturn IP/ISO9660 disc. The firmware issues actual CD commands and SCU DMA operations; the host does not install HLE services in this mode.

**But that ROM still hardcodes the first-read file's LBA, byte length, destination/stack and startup layout** (its current original program is 4096 bytes at ISO LBAs 21–22). It therefore demonstrates only a fixed-media hardware handoff, not firmware-driven discovery of a differently laid-out Saturn disc. The existing **BIOS-less HLE** boot parser can already discover appropriate Saturn IP/ISO9660 metadata, but its host-side parsing/loading is not evidence that firmware can discover and load a program by executing ordinary SH-2/CD instructions.

The next meaningful, bounded step toward future game boot compatibility is to **remove the fixed-disc-layout assumptions from the synthetic external-firmware path** and make the firmware itself read, validate and act on the on-disc boot metadata over the emulated CD hardware. Do not replace or duplicate existing host HLE loading, silently fall back to HLE, or claim stock Sega BIOS/commercial-game support.

## Expected outcome

Implement a **firmware-executed** boot-file discovery/loading routine in the existing original MIT-licensed synthetic BIOS ROM:

1. Read Saturn IP/system-header metadata from the mounted disc through actual scheduled CD requests/data transfers.
2. Read and validate an ISO9660 primary volume descriptor, root-directory record(s) and the **Saturn-defined first-read file selection contract** (follow primary manual requirements; the existing documented HLE path uses the first regular root child / first-read file identifier 2). Do **not** confuse a generic arbitrary executable search with the Saturn boot specification.
3. Obtain the selected file's **actual extent, size, and file layout from disc directory records**, and the executable destination, stack and application entry conditions from **Saturn IP fields** where the specification defines them. In particular, do not treat an IP first-read size field as authoritative if the primary spec instead uses the ISO file record.
4. Stream/transfer the selected bytes using emulated CD commands, host FIFO and/or SCU DMA, respecting scheduling, cancellation and memory bounds. Transfer control to the loaded guest code with a firmware-established stack/context.
5. Pass independently authored native and production browser/Wasm oracles over **several original, differently laid-out discs**, without changing the firmware's executable ROM bytes between variants. The same general discovery path must run for every valid fixture.

This is a **finite, real-hardware-path boot-loader increment**, not a mandate to implement all ISO9660 extensions, every Sega BIOS library, region/security authentication or a complete general-purpose filesystem. Implement the smallest coherent primary-backed set that handles the chosen documented Saturn-compatible cases, including negative cases.

## Context and reproduction

Current checked `main`: `260f1a3fd543faf9d8fca74d221ec69257bbcbd5`. There were no open Issues/PRs at task creation.

Inspect the existing implementation and reproduce its current fixed-layout limitation **before** editing production code:

- [`docs/external-startup.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/external-startup.md): independent ExternalBios startup and literal hardware transaction contract; the current firmware has a **fixed LBA21–22, size 4096** first-read program and fixed private ABI.
- [`docs/validation-issue-83.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/validation-issue-83.md): original 512 KiB firmware/ISO, successful host-independent first handoff and fixed cold-reset medium retention.
- [`tests/fixtures/external-startup.s`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/tests/fixtures/external-startup.s), [`external-startup-disc.s`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/tests/fixtures/external-startup-disc.s), [`build_external_startup.py`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/tests/fixtures/build_external_startup.py), [`tests/external_startup.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/tests/external_startup.rs), [`scripts/external-startup.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/external-startup.mjs).
- [`src/disc.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/src/disc.rs), [`src/media.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/src/media.rs), [`src/cd.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/src/cd.rs) and [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): HLE already parses IP and bounded ISO9660 first-read layouts, including selected extended-attribute/interleaving cases; **that parser must not perform the firmware's work**.
- [`docs/hardware-conformance.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware-conformance.md), [`src/hle/README.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/src/hle/README.md): CD commands and BIOS/CD services are partial; ExternalBios and HLE modes must remain separate.
- [Saturn Disc Format Standards ST-040-R4](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-040-R4-051795.pdf), [Saturn Boot ROM User's Manual ST-079B-R3](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-079B-R3-011895.pdf), the [CD I/F reference](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-162-062094.pdf), and ISO9660/ECMA-119 directory/volume record definitions. Verify exact sections/revisions and reconcile apparent contradictions, rather than treating a fixture convention as hardware truth.

A useful inherited-main negative control is a valid disc whose first-read file **moves to another extent** and whose size changes while the BIOS ROM stays byte-for-byte unchanged. The inherited fixed-LBA path must fail an unchanged independently specified guest/loader oracle. Verify the failure source rather than manufacturing a failure by deliberately corrupting the entire disc.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Primary-derived boot contract:** document actual Saturn IP/first-read discovery and entry rules, PVD/root traversal, ISO record extent/length/flags, LBA-to-FAD conversion, CD read/transfer protocol and reset/error behavior, with exact primary citations. Distinguish Saturn first-read semantics from optional generic file browsing. Note unsupported standard formats clearly rather than assuming them valid.
- [ ] **Real firmware-side discovery:** extend the original MIT synthetic BIOS's **SH-2 instructions** (or an original firmware-executed routine in ROM) to read the relevant disc metadata through scheduled CD/MMIO operations, parse the required bytes in emulated RAM and derive the selected file location/size from actual records. No host parser, Rust/JS special case, ROM-signature check, test-only skip, preloaded file, private MMIO backdoor or hardcoded fixture extent may supply decisions/results in ExternalBios. Fixed standard descriptor positions, e.g. sector 16, are permissible where specified by the ISO format; a fixed *first-read-file* extent is not.
- [ ] **Layout-independent executable handoff:** load the full specified file (including non-sector-aligned final length) into a valid destination derived from documented IP fields, establish stack/entry, preserve bounds/alignment and jump to genuine fetched instructions. Prevent unsafe overlap with the executing firmware's live RAM, vector/stack workspace and reserved addresses. Preserve correct CD data integrity, FIFO/SCU DMA completion and error handling.
- [ ] **Multiple independently reproducible valid discs:** use the **same firmware binary** against at least **three** original MIT-licensed ISO9660/Saturn-IP fixtures whose first-read file extents, directory padding/position, program lengths (including a non-sector-multiple) and at least one valid IP destination or stack field differ. If an interleaved/extended-attribute case is included, honor the exact documented addressing semantics; otherwise mark it explicitly as outside this increment. Include a multi-sector directory/descriptor boundary where practical. Native and production Wasm must compute the same independent literal results for each.
- [ ] **Real bytes, not canned results:** inspect/compare complete executable bytes and guest-computed RAM/PC/SP/context markers, CD command/status/interrupt/DMA records and any relevant Canvas output, using expectations independent of emulator helpers. Mutating source file bytes and file-record extents must change actual transferred instructions/results. Omitted connection/command or changed first-read selection must not accidentally succeed.
- [ ] **Negative and boundary controls:** malformed PVD/root/extent/size, wrong or missing first-read regular file, zero/oversized/excessively fragmented or out-of-medium reads, incorrect IP header/region area layout, no medium, aborted/read-error/reset-in-progress and an invalid/different BIOS selection must fail explicitly and safely **without executing stale or partially loaded data**. Accept only document-supported variants; unsupported formats must have bounded clear errors rather than silent truncation or unbounded loops.
- [ ] **Clock/state equivalence:** use real scheduled CD operations and bus grants with proper HIRQ/SCU acknowledgement, retained medium, fresh transfers and once-only effects across cold boot, SYSRES and restart. Compare advancement chunks (1/3/17/10000 where applicable) and passive inspection. Ensure fetching metadata doesn't race a pending command or DMA, and no host-side shortcut advances time or manufactures guest success.
- [ ] **Mode and privacy isolation:** the native ExternalBios and browser 'User-provided BIOS' paths require a genuine selected ROM and selected medium; the browser supports choosing them in either order, local bytes remain private, and restart keeps selections as in #83. HLE Star Collector/Prism Courier/Hardware Lab behavior and auto-bootstrap remain unchanged. No Sega BIOS image or commercial media may be committed, uploaded or required.
- [ ] **Registered native/Wasm tests:** update fixture generation/checks, the relevant native tests, browser group/shard registry, failure-propagation and artifact coverage gates; include the complete 64/69/70-group lineage rather than dropping older tests. Preserve full-data pixel/PCM, security/privacy and hardware trace assertions, and all current tests while adding coverage. Document hashes and independent inherited-main negative controls.
- [ ] **Final implementation passes automation:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native and Wasm Clippy with `-D warnings`, `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, `node --test scripts/ci-runner.test.mjs` and complete `npm run test:browser` must pass, along with the required PR GitHub Actions checks. Record actual counts, failures corrected, what was run and what is pending. No flaky skips, blanket retries, human approval or manual hardware tests.
- [ ] **Implementation and honest documentation:** update `docs/external-startup.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/hardware-conformance.md` and a dedicated `docs/validation-issue-85.md` (adjust to the assigned Issue number). Explicitly record which metadata formats and layouts firmware can actually discover, remaining CD/HLE/BIOS ABI gaps, and the boundaries of synthesized boot evidence. Do not claim original Sega BIOS, authenticated retail boot, broad homebrew support or commercial-game compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional original raw BIN/CUE cases, directory extensions, multi-extent files, interleaved contents, alternate region/PLL profiles and richer real-time CD stress tests are valuable only if they can be fully validated without derailing the focused boot-file-discovery increment. Unsupported optional cases may stay explicit follow-up work. Hardware manuals and already licensed fixtures are sufficient; **no physical console, actual Sega BIOS, proprietary game disc, human sign-off or live Pages inspection is required**.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Full automated behavior and PR checks are pre-merge requirements; ordinary main-only Pages deployment remains governed by the existing artifact and validation gates, without additional human acceptance.

## Related work

Follow-up to [#83](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/issues/83) / [#84](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/84). Related to #17's remaining Saturn hardware and firmware-compatibility scope. Completing this issue proves a **synthetic, firmware-executed layout-independent boot**, not general or retail compatibility.
